g.text: In Apache Kafka, "CRC" refers to "Cyclic Redundancy Check," a method used to detect data corruption

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: by attaching a checksum to each message.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: This allows the system to verify whether a message has been altered

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: during transmission or storage by comparing the calculated checksum with the stored one;

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: essentially ensuring data integrity within the Kafka cluster.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: # If your goal is to optimize sending data to brokers using the Sticky Partitioning Strategy,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: the producer will look at how fast the current set of brokers are responding to requests to store data

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: and adapt to send more data to the faster brokers.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: which says that if a request to a partition takes longer than this timeout,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: then that partition will be ignored, and data will be sent elsewhere.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.RoundRobinPartitioner: This partitioning strategy is that each record

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: in a series of consecutive records will be sent to a different partition(no matter if the ‘key’ is provided or not),

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: until we run out of partitions and start over again.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Note: There’s a known issue that will cause uneven distribution when new batch is created.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Please check KAFKA-9965 for more detail

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: #Record Assignment: When a producer sends records to a Kafka topic without specified keys,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: the sticky partitioner assigns all such records to a single partition

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: for a defined duration or until the batch is filled(or linger.ms). This approach helps to create larger batches of records.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: #Switching Partitions: Once a batch is fully formed or other conditions (like the linger.ms timeout) are met,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: the sticky partitioner can switch to another partition, maintaining a balance over time

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: by eventually spreading records evenly across all partitions.

Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: In Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), Transparent Huge Pages (THP) is a memory management feature that aims to improve system performance

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: by using larger memory pages (2MB) instead of the default smaller pages (4KB). THP is enabled by default in RHEL and

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: automatically manages the allocation of these huge pages, unlike traditional Huge Pages which need to be reserved manually.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: disabling THP in RHEL is recommended for Kafka broker deployments to prevent potential performance issues related to latency and memory management.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: This step helps ensure that the deployment can handle high throughput and low latency, which are critical requirements for Kafka workloads.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: You can check the current THP status using the command: cat /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: If you experience performance issues with THP, you can disable it using the same command, changing

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: the value to never. You can also disable it permanently by modifying bootloader configuration.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Set socket.request.max.bytes in each broker's server.properties file. Be careful not to exceed the maximum value found in the step above

g.text: num.recovery.threads.per.data.dir -- the number of recovery threads per data directory at startup and shutdown. For JBOD, set this to 1; for RAID, set this to the number of disks in the RAID array.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: message.max.bytes -- the maximum message size. Anything higher than 1M is strongly discouraged.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: replica.fetch.max.bytes -- must be higher than message.max.bytes.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Also, the JVM heap size must be larger than (replica.fetch.max.bytes *

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Does num.io.threads equal the number of cores? Setting this to the number of cores on the broker will increase throughput.

g.text: If you configure multiple data directories, the broker places a new partition in the path with the least number of partitions currently stored. Each partition will be entirely in one of the data directories.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: If data is not well balanced among partitions, this can lead to load imbalance among disks. RAID 10 is recommended as the best “sleep at night” option for most use cases. It provides improved read and write performance,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: data protection (ability to tolerate disk failures), and fast rebuild times

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Kafka relies heavily on the filesystem for storing and caching messages. All data is immediately written to a persistent log on the filesystem without necessarily flushing to disk. In effect this just means that it is transferred

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: into the kernel’s pagecache. You need sufficient memory to buffer active readers and writers. You can do a back-of-the-envelope estimate of memory needs by assuming you want to be able to buffer for 30 seconds and compute your memory need as write_throughput * 30.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: A machine with 64 GB of RAM is a decent choice, but 32 GB machines are not uncommon. Less than 32 GB tends to be counterproductive (you end up needing many, many small machines).

g.text: How to set - You can set this to the same value as the number of CPU cores

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Explanation / Details - This will allow you to use all of the brokers CPU cores

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: for IO tasks which can unblock it if IO is its bottleneck. Setting this to a value

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: How to set - You can set this to the same value as the number of CPU cores,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: but I’d usually set it a bit lower

g.text: tasks which can unblock it if IO is its bottleneck. Setting this to a value higher

g.text: Explanation - Having too many partitions per broker has been shown to

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: drastically impact throughput. The num.replica.fetchers configuration option sets

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: the number of replica fetchers the broker will create PER other broker in the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: cluster. Meaning if we set it to two and there are two other brokers in our

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: cluster our broker will spin up two fetchers for each of them for a total of four.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: This configuration option has been shown to help reduce the impact of excessive

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: How to set - Trial at 0, 512, 1048576 and then iterate based on the throughput

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: and end-to-end latency achieved at each level

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Explanation - By setting this value above 0 you can force the fetcher thread to

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: wait more time (up to replica.fetch.wait.max.ms) before it completes the fetch

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: request. Less fetch requests mean less load on the cluster which improves

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: throughput and end-to-end latency. This may increase the end-to-end latency for

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: some of the records but the improved performance may lead to better end-to-

g.text: How to set - There are many ways depending on how it’s installed, but one place

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: is /proc/sys/fs/file-max and it should be set to at least 200,000

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Explanation - The Kafka broker creates a large number of files which it must

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: keep open at any time. By default the OS only allows 1024 per process which

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: isn’t enough for a normal broker. If this limit is hit the broker will immediately

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Explanation - Any data swapped to disk will require disk IO to read from in the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: future rather than a read from memory. This operation is in the magnitude of a

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: thousand times slower and as such swapping should always be disabled for Big

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Data applications. Certain OS functionality behaves poorly with vm.swappiness=0

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: which is why we set it to the lowest value we can without setting it to zero.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Explanation - The default of this value is 10 which means once 10% of the OS

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: memory is “dirty” meaning it has buffered writes intended for the disk but not

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: yet written them to disk, it will begin writing them to disk. The reason we set

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: this lower is because Kafka is largely append only so we are going to be modifying

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: the same piece of data a lot before writing it out. We also want to avoid hitting

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: vm.dirty_ratio at all cost, so setting this value lower can help in achieving this.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Explanation - The default of this value is 20 which means once 20% of the OS

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: memory is “dirty” meaning it has buffered writes intended for the disk but not

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: yet written them to disk, it will trigger blocking IO and wait until the data has

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: been written to disk before continuing. We never want Kafka blocking on writing

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: to disk as it is thousands of times slower than a write to memory.
